title: Firms' board diversity and radical innovation: mediation mechanism of firms' attention to digital transformation
summary: This study integrates board information processing theory with the attention-based view to examine how board diversity affects radical innovation through an organizational attention pathway. We argue that board diversity shapes firms' attention to digital transformation (FADT), which in turn promotes radical innovation, and that industry competition conditions this process by heightening the urgency of attending to digital opportunities. Using longitudinal data from 2556 publicly listed Chinese firms from 2008 to 2019, we find that board diversity has an inverted U-shaped relationship with FADT and that FADT positively affects radical innovation. FADT thus mediates the inverted U-shaped relationship between board diversity and radical innovation, producing an inverted U-shaped indirect effect. Industry competition strengthens the relationship between board diversity and FADT, making this indirect effect more pronounced in competitive environments. These findings clarify how board diversity contributes to radical innovation by directing organizational attention toward digital transformation and show why moderate diversity is especially valuable when firms face strong competitive pressure.

title: Modern Slavery in Supply Chains: A Framing Perspective on Managerial Responses to Transparency Legislation
summary: ABSTRACT Innovative legislation aspires for an extra‐jurisdictional effect on modern slavery in supply chains through increased transparency. Evidence to date suggests that firms are not rising to this challenge, and, if anything, mandatory reporting practices are coalescing around superficial reports decoupled from policy objectives. To decide how the regulatory regime should best be adapted, it is important to understand not just the organizational‐level response but also the underlying managerial attitudes and behavior on which substantive practical action depends. The study utilized a photo elicitation method with 47 managers drawn from eight large UK construction firms. Framing theory was utilized to reveal four distinct managerial mindsets, each with different implications for policy and practice. These variants suggest that a one‐size‐fits‐all policy approach is suboptimal. Policy combining rewards and penalties, tailored to each framing group, is likely to be the most expedient in quickly improving managerial behavior. The existence of inconsistent framing within firms suggests that strategic policies are not being effectively embedded in managerial practice. In turn, this limits the impact that focal firms have in improving labor practices across multiple tiers of their supply chains. Reporting entities should not be treated as cohesive, unitary entities by stakeholders.

title: Does digital and non-digital technology integration improve corporate supply chain resilience?
summary: The in-depth integration of the digital economy and the real economy can effectively enhance the resilience and vitality of economic development. This study explores the impact of digital and non-digital technology integration ( DNTI ) on supply chain resilience and its mechanisms from a micro perspective. The findings show that DNTI can significantly improve supply chain resilience, and the results still hold after endogeneity and robustness test. The mechanism analysis shows that DNTI enhances supply chain resilience by reducing corporate financing constraints, improving information disclosure quality, and broadening knowledge breadth. This effect is stronger for firms in less marketization degress, more competitive industries, higher levels of internal control and higher supply chain concentration. Overall, these findings can provide new insights into coping with supply chain risks and strategic adjustments.

title: Supply chain resilience prediction and industrial economic shock transmission path analysis integrating knowledge graphs and deep reinforcement learning
summary: Mounting geopolitical frictions, trade disputes and public health emergencies have exposed structural fragilities in global supply chains, yet the tools built to anticipate those fragilities still keep relational reasoning and adaptive decision-making apart. This paper joins them. We assemble a multimodal supply chain knowledge graph spanning 1.86 million entities and 23 relation types drawn from input–output tables, customs records, corporate disclosures and a curated disruption case repository, then design an attention-augmented R-GCN encoder that compresses topology, attributes and temporal disruption signals into resilience-sensitive embeddings. On that representation the proposed KG-PPO algorithm couples a clipped policy objective with cascade-aware reward shaping, so that interpretable transmission paths emerge alongside the resilience forecast. Experiments on automotive, electronic information and pharmaceutical chains benchmark KG-PPO against eleven baselines, among them three recent supply chain graph models and information-matched variants that receive the same graph features as the proposed agent. Averaged over five seeds, KG-PPO lowers MAE by 18.3% and lifts AUC by 3.5 points relative to the strongest baseline; both gaps survive paired testing with Holm correction, while several mid-ranked baselines cannot be told apart from one another. A streaming experiment over a twelve-week crisis window shows that incremental graph updates hold the rolling error near its pre-crisis level at roughly a twelfth of the cost of full retraining, and a six-factor sweep places the reported configuration on a flat optimum rather than a knife-edge. Rare-earth refining and semiconductor foundries emerge as the deepest chokepoints under the shock protocol used here, and strategy simulations trace the cost-resilience frontier under inventory redundancy, multi-source procurement and capacity flexibility. The ontology schema, the per-seed records behind every table and the code that regenerates every figure are released with the paper.

AI.abstract_translation: 不断加剧的地缘政治摩擦、贸易争端与突发公共卫生事件，暴露了全球供应链的结构性脆弱性，然而为预判这些脆弱性而构建的工具，却始终将关系推理与适应性决策相互割裂。本文将其合而为一。我们构建了一个多模态供应链知识图谱，涵盖186万个实体与23种关系类型，数据源自投入产出表、海关记录、企业信息披露以及一个经过整理的扰动案例库，随后设计了一个注意力增强的R-GCN编码器，将拓扑结构、属性与时间性扰动信号压缩为对韧性敏感的嵌入表示。在该表示之上，所提出的KG-PPO算法将裁剪后的策略目标与级联感知的奖励塑形相结合，从而使可解释的传导路径与韧性预测同时涌现。在汽车、电子信息与医药产业链上的实验中，KG-PPO与十一个基线模型进行了基准比较，其中包括三个近期的供应链图模型，以及接收与所提出智能体相同图特征的信息匹配变体。在五个随机种子上取平均，KG-PPO相较最强基线将MAE降低了18.3%，并将AUC提升了3.5个百分点；两项差距在采用Holm校正的配对检验下均得以保持，而若干排名居中的基线之间则无法相互区分。一个覆盖十二周危机窗口的流式实验显示，增量式图更新可将滚动误差维持在危机前水平附近，其成本约为完全重训练成本的十二分之一，而六因素扫描表明所报告的配置处于平坦最优区域，而非临界尖峰。在本文所用的冲击协议下，稀土精炼与半导体代工成为最深的瓶颈环节，策略模拟则刻画了在库存冗余、多源采购与产能灵活性下的成本—韧性前沿。本体模式（ontology schema）、每张表格背后的逐种子记录，以及可复现每张图的代码，均随本文一并发布。

title: The Study on Green Finance Awareness Among Lecturers in Politeknik Ungku Omar
summary: Green finance has become a critical mechanism for addressing environmental challenges through sustainable economic development. As climate concerns grow, digital tools are giving green finance an advance. Fintech innovations are making sustainable investments easier to understand, quicker to access and open to more people empowering communities to build a better tomorrow. This study investigates the intersection of digital transformation, Fintech and green finance in terms of lecturers' awareness and perception at Politeknik Ungku Omar, Malaysia. The main objectives were to assess the level of green finance awareness, evaluate the influence of digital transformation and examine the role of Fintech in promoting sustainability. A quantitative research design was employed involving a structured questionnaire distributed to 100 lecturers across various departments. Data collection covered demographic details, awareness of green finance, perceptions of digital transformation and the role of Fintech in sustainability. Descriptive statistics, reliability testing and correlation analysis were conducted using Statistical software. The findings revealed high awareness of green finance, positive perception of digital transformation in finance and strong belief in Fintech's role in sustainability. Cronbach’s alpha values indicated high reliability. Significant positive correlations were observed between awareness, digital transformation and Fintech involvement, affirming the integrated role of digital tools in promoting sustainable financial practices. These findings can guide strategic planning for educational, financial and governmental institutions obligated to building environmentally responsible and digitally forward-looking economies.

title: Financial Reporting Quality and Its Impact on Firm Performance: A Study of Corporate Governance
summary: The study investigated the effect of corporate governance practices on financial reporting quality in Nigerian Deposit Money Banks with special focus on selected banks in Warri, Delta State. The growing number of financial misstatements, corporate scandals and stakeholder concerns regarding transparency have created the need for effective corporate governance mechanisms that ensure the integrity and reliability of financial reports. The study examined the effect of internal control system, board structure, ethical standards and regulatory compliance on financial reporting quality in Nigeria Deposit Money Banks. The study adopted a survey research design. Data was collected thru administration of structured questionnaires on employes of selected Deposit Money Banks in Warri. The study was guided by corporate governance principles which emphasize accountability, transparency, responsibility and fairness in the operations and financial disclosures of organizations. Results indicated that the internal control system has a positive and significant effect on the quality of financial reporting. This implies that the higher the level of the control system, the more accurate, reliable and credible the financial statements are. The study also found that the structure of the board has a significant effect on the quality of financial reporting, implying that competent, independent and organized boards are capable of providing strong oversight which enhances financial reporting practices. Moreover, ethical standards had a statistically significant positive effect on financial reporting quality by improving transparency, accountability and integrity of financial transactions and disclosures. Furthermore, it was also found that regulatory compliance had a significant and positive effect on the quality of financial reporting. Thus, adherence to statutory requirements and regulatory guidelines enhances the confidence of stakeholders and improves the credibility of financial reports. In view of these findings, the study concludes that corporate governance is important to the improvement of financial reporting quality in Nigerian Deposit Money Banks. The study suggests that banks should improve their governance structures thru continuous enhancement of internal control systems, board effectiveness, ethical conduct, and compliance with regulatory standards set by relevant authorities.

title: CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AND PROFITABILITY OF DEPOSIT MONEY BANKS IN NIGERIA
summary: Effective corporate governance has become a key concept in modern banking systems, which determines how financial institutions manage risks and deliver value. Therefore, this study examined the implications of corporate governance on the profitability of deposit money banks (DMBs) in Nigeria. The study analyzed how audit committee size, board size, and independent board members (independent variables) affect profitability, as determined by stock returns (dependent variable). A longitudinal correlational research design was employed to determine the relationships among the specified variables between 2009 and 2024. The population comprised 13 DMBs listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group with 12 of them selected as sample size. Data were gathered from the audited financial statements of the sampled banks. A multiple regression analysis technique was employed to measure the associations among the variables under study. Audit committee size (β = 0.883, p < 0.05) and board size (β = 0.026, p < 0.05) positively and significantly affect banks' profitability. Independent board members (β = -0.040, p > 0.05) have a negative but statistically insignificant effect on profitability. The study concluded that proper corporate governance contributes to better financial performance among banks. Therefore, it was recommended that deposit money banks improve their governance mechanisms, particularly through an appropriately structured board, a more effective audit committee and a larger board for greater financial performance and institutional integrity.

title: Supplier Financial Distress and Manufacturing Disruption
summary: Supplier financial distress is not only a credit problem. In strategic manufacturing supply chains, deteriorating liquidity can reduce maintenance, labor retention, quality control, capacity, and delivery reliability before legal default occurs. This review integrates seventy peer-reviewed studies from bankruptcy prediction, corporate finance, operations management, production-network economics, supply-chain resilience, machine learning, and forecast evaluation. It finds that conventional accounting scores are useful baselines but are too slow and too detached from buyer-specific exposure to serve as complete disruption warnings. A defensible early-warning system must estimate two linked hazards: the probability that a supplier enters financial distress and the probability that this condition produces a material disruption for a particular buyer. It must then combine those probabilities with substitutability, network position, inventory cover, recovery time, and consequence. The review proposes a dynamic, interpretable architecture using financial ratios, market indicators, payment behavior, operational signals, textual disclosures, macroeconomic conditions, and multi-tier network features. It also specifies calibrated outputs, escalation thresholds, governance controls, and an empirical validation design for strategic US supply chains. The central conclusion is that prediction becomes valuable only when it creates sufficient lead time for a proportionate and economically justified intervention.

title: Relationship between IFRS Adoption and Financial Reporting Quality in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates
summary: Purpose: This study examines the effect of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) adoption on financial reporting quality (FRQ) among non-financial listed firms in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Financial reporting quality is assessed using two complementary measures: accrual-based earnings management and timely loss recognition Design/Methodology/Approach: The study employs quantitative panel data from non-financial listed firms in Saudi Arabia and the UAE, covering the periods surrounding IFRS adoption in both countries. IFRS adoption is measured using a dummy variable distinguishing the pre- and post-adoption periods, while financial reporting quality is measured through AEM and TLR. Dynamic panel estimation is applied to account for the persistence of financial reporting quality and potential econometric issues. Findings: The empirical findings indicate that IFRS adoption significantly improves financial reporting quality. Specifically, IFRS adoption is associated with a significant reduction in accrual-based earnings management, suggesting lower managerial discretion over reported earnings. IFRS adoption also has a significant positive effect on timely loss recognition, indicating greater accounting conservatism and more timely recognition of economic losses following IFRS adoption. Implications/Originality/Value: In this comparative study of Saudi Arabia and the UAE, we are able to show how IFRS adoption leads to less earnings management and increased timeliness of recognizing losses. As a result, our results indicate to all interested parties that implementing IFRS does improve the quality of financial reporting.

title: Rana Plaza to Regulation: Rethinking Voluntary CSR in Global Supply Chains
summary: A critical watershed in Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and business accountability debates was marked on 24 April 2013 when the Rana Plaza building collapsed, killing over 1,100 garment workers. This is a profound example of a power imbalance driving the prioritisation of profit over human rights. When the weak governance frameworks relying on self-regulation are considered, the disaster should be perceived as foreseeable. The structural limitations of voluntary CSR mechanisms used to prevent systemic labour and safety violations in global supply chains, which persisted within these frameworks, were exposed. Using the Rana Plaza case study, this article places the conduct of Bangladeshi state authorities within the framework of international human rights law and the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs) by examining the distribution of responsibility between factory owners and multinational brands. The analysis demonstrates how state regulatory failure, corporate practices, and the suppression of collective labour rights combined to create the conditions in which employers coerced workers into life-threatening environments. It further analyses post-Rana Plaza regulatory developments, including the Bangladesh Accord on Fire and Building Safety and mandatory Human Rights Due Diligence (HRDD) regimes emerging in Europe. Whilst the progress these initiatives represent is acknowledged, for workers’ rights to be adequately protected in global supply chains, there must be a decisive shift from voluntary CSR to binding, enforceable legal accountability.

title: The Study of the Impact Mechanism of R&D Expense Super-deduction on Green Innovation of High-tech Enterprises in the Context of the Digital Economy
summary: As the digital economy improves by leaps and bounds, new factor conditions are provided for corporate green innovation. In the meantime, the R&D expense super-deduction policy has become a vital fiscal and tax instrument for incentivizing high-tech enterprises to conduct low-carbon technology R&D. Nevertheless, existing research rarely places the digital economy, the super-deduction policy, as well as corporate green innovation within the same framework, and analyses of transmission paths and differentiated policy effects still need improvement. Against this background, this research selects panel data of A-share listed high-tech enterprises from 2019 to 2023 as the sample, and then constructs two-way fixed effects and mediation effect models, and empirically examines the impact of the R&D expense super-deduction on green innovation of high-tech enterprises and its internal transmission mechanism. Further, Heterogeneity analysis is conducted from three dimensions: ownership nature, regional distribution, and firm size. The results suggest that the R&D expense super-deduction reinforces green innovation in high-tech enterprises, R&D intensity plays a partial mediating role in this process, and the policy incentive effect is heterogeneous, being more significant in non-state-owned, eastern-region, and small-scale high-tech enterprises. This paper supplements micro-level evidence on the intersection of fiscal and tax incentives and corporate green innovation, and provides references for the government, in order to implement differentiated tax policies and for enterprises to conduct green R&D.

title: Internal Corporate Social Responsibility and Employee Burnout: The Complementary Role of Responsible Leadership
summary: ABSTRACT This study synthesizes the literature on how internal corporate social responsibility (CSR) is associated with employee burnout and examines responsible leadership as an emerging complementary condition. Using a Scopus‐based mixed review design, the study combines bibliometric mapping of 68 records with a PRISMA‐guided qualitative synthesis of 16 studies. The findings indicate that burnout and CSR constitute the conceptual core of the field, whereas responsible leadership remains less consolidated. Internal CSR practices, including organizational support, fairness, work‐life balance, wellbeing benefits, and psychologically safe climates, are consistently associated with lower burnout or emotional exhaustion. The review develops an evidence‐informed interpretive framework organized around three pathways—resources, relationships, and meaning—through which internal CSR and responsible leadership may shape burnout‐related outcomes. The article contributes by reframing burnout as an internal sustainability outcome and by identifying a focused research agenda for sustainable and psychologically healthy workplaces.

title: Capabilities Before Commitments? Green‐Innovation Persistence, ESG Performance, and Net‐Zero Pledges in China and Europe
summary: ABSTRACT We examine to what extent firm‐level green patenting is persistent, whether ESG performance and net‐zero commitments condition this persistence, and whether these associations differ between China and Europe. Using firm‐level panel data for Chinese and European listed companies from 2011 to 2020, we estimate dynamic firm fixed‐effects models with sector‐year and country‐year controls. We find that green patenting is strongly persistent among Chinese firms and significantly less persistent among European firms, revealing pronounced regional heterogeneity that is consistent with, though not attributable solely to, institutional differences. In China, overall ESG performance strengthens the translation of prior green‐innovation capability into subsequent patenting, and the environmental‐pillar interaction is likewise positive and significant. European evidence is consistent with firms possessing stronger prior green‐innovation capability being more likely to adopt net‐zero pledges. A positive post‐adoption interaction is consistent with pledges reinforcing existing capabilities, but it is driven by a single treated firm‐year and therefore remains only suggestive. These conditional associations are consistent with accumulated technological capability, proxied by prior green patenting, being the key conditioning factor for subsequent green innovation in our samples. ESG performance may strengthen the deployment of that capability, whereas the role of formal net‐zero commitments remains suggestive given the limited European treatment window. For policymakers and corporate leaders, the results imply that disclosure requirements and pledge frameworks should be combined with sustained support for green R&D, specialized human capital and implementation capacity.

title: The Role of Agile Governance in Achieving Sustainable Digital Transformation: Toward a Sustainable Agile Governance (SAG) Framework for Boards and Senior Management
summary: Digital transformation programmes are increasingly judged not only on return on investment and delivery velocity but on their long-term, sustainable impact on shareholders, employees, communities and the environment. Prevailing governance processes remain largely hierarchical and stage-gated, poorly suited to adaptive, data-driven, broad-based accountability, while agile approaches developed for delivery teams are rarely extended to board and senior-management practice — producing a “governance gap” in which delivery teams sprint while oversight plods. This paper examines the relationship between agile governance and sustainability in digital transformation and proposes a Sustainable Agile Governance (SAG) Framework for boards and senior management. Drawing on a structured literature synthesis across corporate governance, agile management, ESG reporting and digital transformation (46 sources), together with an illustrative thematic, maturity and comparative analysis, the paper finds that: (1) agile governance accelerates decision-making but does not by itself improve sustainability outcomes; (2) embedding sustainability within governance cadence, rather than layering it on as separate reporting, produces materially better alignment (composite score 4.5 vs. 2.3 for agile-only governance); (3) board-level digital and ESG literacy is a precondition for effective oversight of transformation programmes; and (4) a four-pillar structure — adaptive decision rights, sustainability-linked value, continuous risk and assurance, and stakeholder-centric transparency — is sufficient to operationalise the integration. The paper concludes by presenting the SAG Framework in full, its practical implications for boards, its limitations, and a future research agenda.

title: Determinants of bankers' bounded rational intention toward green and climate finance in post-COVID-19 Bangladesh: an analysis using PLS-SEM
summary: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to examine the relationship between bankers' perspectives and their intention to engage in green and climate financing activities after the COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh. In particular, it examines how do bankers' perspectives on deep ecological awareness, the normative structure of social pressure and environmental innovative technology affect their intentions toward green financing activities? Design/methodology/approach As a genuinely interdisciplinary theme, the idea of bounded rationality has gained substantial popularity in the social sciences, especially in green finance and technology. Based on this understanding, a theoretical framework grounded in the theory of bounded rational planned behavior was established to address the objectives of the present paper. Data were collected from bankers employed by selected commercial banks in Bangladesh following a random sampling procedure and analyzed using the partial least square structural equation modeling technique. Findings The findings show that all of the predictors appear to be robust in predicting the green financing intention of the sampled bankers in Bangladesh. The mediating variables also have significant effects. Practical implications Bankers' deep ecological awareness appeared to be a highly significant predictor of their attitudes toward bounded rational intention based on deep ecological awareness. Similarly, the social normative structure also appears to be a robust antecedent of subjective norms, which influence respondents’ bounded rational intention toward green and climate (G&C) financing. Social implications G&C financing practices can help reduce carbon emissions and other pollutants, thereby improving overall environmental sustainability and ecological conditions. Originality/value Few studies have focused on the G&C financing perspective in Bangladesh. This research is one of the empirical studies that will certainly add value for clients, institutions and policymakers in financing and banking sectors.

title: Research on Enterprise Financial Management Transformation and Risk Prevention and Control under the Background of Digital Economy
summary: With the steady advancement of the digital economy, digital technologies such as big data and artificial intelligence continuously empower the real economy. Traditional financial management relies on post-event accounting and suffers from drawbacks including poor data timeliness. Financial digital transformation has become an inevitable choice for enterprises to strengthen internal control and improve core competitiveness. This paper aims to sort out the driving factors and implementation paths of financial digital transformation, identify new financial risks arising from the transformation and establish a prevention framework. Combined with industrial practice and existing literature, this study adopts inductive analysis to summarize four types of risks, namely data leakage, system operation and maintenance failures, inter-departmental collaboration barriers and cross-border transmission of industrial chain risks, and analyzes their causes. The research finds that financial digital transformation streamlines financial procedures and optimizes corporate resource allocation, yet it also creates new financial risks. Accordingly, this paper constructs a risk prevention and control system from four dimensions: technical operation and maintenance, internal control optimization, organizational collaboration and industrial chain joint defense, helping enterprise financial management shift toward strategic empowerment and value-added management.

title: Blockchain Technology in Accounting and Business: Implications for Financial Reporting, Operational Efficiency, and Firm Performance - A Thematic Review
summary: Blockchain technology is increasingly applied beyond cryptocurrency in accounting and business, but its reported benefits are not realized uniformly across organizations. This study reviews how blockchain-enabled capabilities relate to financial reporting, operational efficiency, and firm performance and identifies the conditions shaping those relationships. A qualitative thematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed articles, conference papers, scholarly books, and related academic publications, with emphasis on studies published between 2017 and 2025. Evidence was synthesized around reporting outcomes, operational efficiency, firm performance, adoption conditions, and implementation challenges. The literature indicates that blockchain can strengthen transaction traceability, information integrity, auditability, coordination, and process automation. These mechanisms are associated with improved reporting transparency, operational efficiency, innovation capability, competitiveness, and selected performance measures. However, technological readiness, managerial support, cybersecurity, interoperability, infrastructure, and regulatory conditions substantially influence implementation outcomes. Blockchain is therefore better understood as a contingent organizational capability whose value depends on complementary organizational and institutional conditions rather than as an automatic source of superior performance.

title: Leaders or Followers? Individual‐Level Sustainability Orientations on Corporate Social Responsibility and Their Theoretical Drivers
summary: ABSTRACT Although the literature on Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) increasingly recognizes the coexistence of multiple theoretical frameworks at the organizational level, little is known about how individual professionals internalize and combine these frameworks in managerial practice. This study fills this gap by analyzing management engineers, who play a key role in translating corporate sustainability strategies into operational decisions. Through a sequential, two‐phase research design, an exploratory analysis based on Principal Component Analysis and K‐means clustering identifies two distinct profiles (Sustainability Leaders and Sustainability Followers) which were subsequently validated through a second questionnaire, in which respondents self‐identified with the profiles and evaluated five organizational theories. The results show that the two groups do not differ in digital skills, which are now widespread across the board, but rather in how they integrate sustainability, stakeholder engagement, and systems thinking into their decisions. A regression analysis reveals that Stakeholder Theory positively explains membership in the Leader profile, while Institutional Theory characterizes the Follower profile. This study contributes to research on CSR by demonstrating that sustainability orientations at the individual level are based on distinct theoretical frameworks, thereby extending the analysis of CSR from organizational strategies to the professionals responsible for their implementation.

title: When risk silences optimism: supply chain disruption risk and the reduction of abnormal managerial tone
summary: Purpose Amid intensifying geopolitical frictions and the trend toward de-globalization, supply chain disruptions have emerged as a salient source of risk for firms, yet their implications for managerial disclosure remain unclear. Our study aims to reveal the impact of supply chain disruption risk on managerial tone management during earnings communication conferences. Design/methodology/approach Using data on China A-share-listed firms from 2006 to 2023, we examine how, why, and when supply chain disruption risk affects abnormal managerial tone during earnings communication conferences. Findings Higher disruption risk reduces abnormal managerial positive tone. The effect operates through two channels: first, managers provide more detailed factual explanations in managerial communication, which increases informational density, as evidenced by shorter and more structured sentences, thereby constraining rhetorical and emotional expression; second, higher supply chain disruption risk raises inventory pressure, which suppresses optimism. The effect is more pronounced when investor questioning is intensive, stock prices are overvalued, or supply chain concentration is high. It is more pronounced among firms with greater trade credit supply or lower excess operating profitability. Originality/value Our study contributes to the literature by linking supply chain disruption risk with strategic disclosure practices, and it offers practical implications for enhancing supply chain resilience, improving disclosure quality, and strengthening market competitiveness.
